title: Accelerating Mixture of Experts Training With Rail Optimized InfiniBand Networking in Crusoe Cloud

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: The talk describes Crusoe Cloud's rail-optimized InfiniBand networking infrastructure that AI engineers use to train large models. Crusoe Cloud is a developer platform providing GPU cluster infrastructure for AI builders. The content focuses on distributed training infrastructure optimization for MoE models. Covers networking topology and NCCL internals but explains them accessibly for a technical audience. Recorded conference presentation at the AI Engineer World's Fair. Includes quantitative real-world benchmarks from Mixtral training on 240 H100 GPUs with measured 14% improvement.

Crusoe Cloud is a developer platform providing GPU cluster infrastructure for AI builders. The content focuses on distributed training infrastructure optimization for MoE models. summary: Ievgen, a product manager at Crusoe Cloud responsible for GPU networking infrastructure, presents their approach to accelerating Mixture of Experts training through rail-optimized InfiniBand networking. Crusoe Cloud is an AI-focused cloud platform built on three pillars: high performance, ease of use for AI engineers, and climate alignment, with data centers in Texas, the north-central US, the East Coast, and a new geothermal-powered facility in Iceland, all powered by renewable and stranded energy for net-zero carbon emissions. The platform offers GPU VMs, CPU instances, local NVMe and persistent block storage, managed file systems, VPC front-end networking, and a dedicated rail-optimized InfiniBand backend. The core problem is that networking consumes approximately 25-30% of training time, during which GPUs idle waiting for data exchange via all-reduce and all-to-all operations. Computation-communication overlap reduces this by only about 10%, still leaving roughly 25% of time on network operations. Traditional fat-tree topologies introduce single choke points and single failure domains at the leaf level. Crusoe's rail-optimized design keeps intra-server communication on NVLink, same-rail traffic one hop through a single leaf, and uses spine switches for cross-rail communication. NVIDIA's PXN feature, introduced in recent NCCL versions, further optimizes cross-rail communication by using the internal NVSwitch within a host to route traffic between GPUs on different rails, maintaining single-hop access. NCCL synthetic tests showed 50% improvement for both small messages (latency) and large messages (bandwidth). However, customers care about real training time rather than synthetic benchmarks. Using the Mixtral open-source sparse MoE model (8 feed-forward blocks, 8x7B parameters) fine-tuned on 240 H100 GPUs, Crusoe measured a 14% training improvement with PXN enabled—a result directly tied to reduced time-to-train and training cost, which generated strong customer excitement.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction & Crusoe Mission
sections.summary: Speaker introduction and overview of Crusoe's mission to align computing with climate by using stranded and renewable energy sources to power data centers, reducing the environmental impact of energy-hungry GPU workloads.

sections.title: Three Pillars & Data Center Locations
sections.summary: Crusoe's platform built on three pillars: high performance for training efficiency, ease of use for AI engineers, and climate alignment targeting net-zero emissions. Data centers located in Texas, north-central US, East Coast, and a new geothermal-powered facility in Iceland.

sections.title: Platform Overview & Customers
sections.summary: Crusoe Cloud offerings include GPU VMs, CPU instances, local NVMe and persistent block storage, managed file systems, VPC front-end networking, and rail-optimized InfiniBand backend. CLI, APIs, and GUI provided. Customers include Together AI and Bosen AI.

sections.title: Distributed Training Challenges
sections.summary: In distributed training, networking consumes 25-30% of training time with GPUs idling during data exchange. Computation-communication overlap reduces this by only ~10%, leaving ~25% still spent on network, motivating the need for optimized cluster networking.

sections.title: Rail-Optimized Topology Introduction
sections.summary: Traditional fat-tree topologies create single choke points and failure domains. Crusoe's rail-optimized design uses NVLink for intra-server communication, single-leaf one-hop paths for same-rail traffic, and spine switches for cross-rail traffic, reducing hops between GPUs.

sections.title: PXN Feature & Cross-Rail Optimization
sections.summary: NVIDIA's PXN feature in recent NCCL versions enables cross-rail GPU communication via the internal NVSwitch within a host, maintaining single-hop access across different rails. NCCL synthetic tests showed 50% improvement for both small messages (latency) and large messages (bandwidth).

sections.title: Real-World MoE Training Results & Conclusion
sections.summary: Customers care about real training time, not synthetic benchmarks. Using the Mixtral open-source sparse MoE model (8 feed-forward blocks, 8x7B parameters) fine-tuned on 240 H100 GPUs, Crusoe measured 14% training improvement with PXN enabled—directly tied to reduced time-to-train and cost. Speaker concludes and opens for Q&A.

limitations: Even with computation-communication overlap, ~25% of training time still spent on networking
Traditional fat-tree topology introduces single choke points and single failure domains at the leaf level
NCCL synthetic benchmark improvements do not directly translate to equivalent real-world training gains
